1 · Intro

When to use it.

When no existing report answers your question, you can build an OTBI analysis from a subject area.

Start from the smallest set of columns that answers the question, and test it against records you know.

Use this whenNo catalog or Playbook report gives you the columns or filters you need.

2 · Walk through

Step by step.

Follow along in Oracle BI. Check off each step as you go.

Watch-outs

  • Hiding a column is not security. Data security comes from Oracle roles, and every viewer sees only what their roles allow.
  • If you do not see Create > Analysis, you may not have a BI author role.
  • Open item: confirm which BI roles HCMs have, who can publish to Shared Folders > Custom, and the request process for new shared reports.

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

  • Oracle: Create Your First Analysis (OTBI) (opens in a new tab)
  • Oracle: HCM Subject Areas for Transactional Business Intelligence (opens in a new tab)

3 · Knowledge check

Check your understanding.

Three questions. You get feedback on each answer. All three right completes the course.

Q1What is the first choice when you create an OTBI analysis?

Q2You hide the salary column in an analysis you share. Is salary data now secured?

Q3Where should an analysis you built for your own use be saved?

Keep it handy.

HCM Academy job aid · Document Records & Reporting

Reporting 301

Use when: No catalog or Playbook report gives you the columns or filters you need. · System: Oracle BI (OTBI)

  1. Create a new analysis and pick a subject area.
  2. Add only the columns you need on the Criteria tab.
  3. Add filters to limit rows.
  4. Add prompts if others will run it for different values.
  5. Check results against known records.
  6. Save to My Folders.

Watch-outs

  • Hiding a column is not security. Data security comes from Oracle roles, and every viewer sees only what their roles allow.
  • If you do not see Create > Analysis, you may not have a BI author role.
  • Open item: confirm which BI roles HCMs have, who can publish to Shared Folders > Custom, and the request process for new shared reports.
